findings.title: Computed zod keys from `.toString()` create literal bogus keys, schema does not do what the comments say
findings.body: `[z.string().toString()]` evaluates to a fixed string such as "[object Object]" or "ZodString", not a wildcard key. The schema therefore requires a numeric property with that literal name, and the second computed key is another literal. No real token response will contain that property. When credential sync is enabled, `safeParse` fails for every response and "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned" is thrown. A real approach would be `z.object({access_token: z.string()}).passthrough()` plus a custom expiry check.

findings.title: Placeholder refresh_token written into the schema's result data and persisted
findings.body: If `refresh_token` is missing, it is set to the literal string "refresh_token". Callers such as Salesforce and Zoom then store it in the credential. A fake refresh token may later be sent to the provider on non-synced paths and fail with invalid_grant. It also mutates `data` typed as an arbitrary schema output. Further, `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token` is accessed on a union type where the property may not exist, which is a type error.

findings.title: parseRefreshTokenResponse result (a SafeParse object) saved as the credential key
findings.body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the `{success, data}` safeParse result, not the parsed data. The code stores that whole object as `key` in `prisma.credential.update`. This corrupts the Google credential: the stored value becomes `{success:true,data:{...}}`, and subsequent `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` fails. Use `.data`.

findings.title: Sync endpoint response is a fetch Response, but code reads `res.data`
findings.body: When credential sync is enabled, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a raw fetch `Response`. Here it is read as `res?.data.access_token` (a gaxios shape), so `data` is undefined and this throws. The error is swallowed by the catch, which returns the old auth, so the token is never refreshed. The response body is never `.json()`-parsed.

findings.title: Sync fetch has no auth, no error handling, and returns inconsistent shapes across callers
findings.body: The POST to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` carries no authentication/secret header, so the endpoint cannot verify the caller. A non-OK response is returned as-is. The helper returns a fetch `Response` on the sync path but whatever `refreshFunction` returns otherwise (axios response, hubspot token object, googleapis res). Callers such as hubspot (expects a token object), zoho (`.data`), and google (`.data`) break on the sync path.

findings.title: Salesforce refresh now unconditionally performed and `prisma` is not imported
findings.body: The new token refresh code calls `prisma.credential.update`, but `prisma` is never imported in this file, so it is a ReferenceError at runtime and fails type-check. The refresh also runs on every client construction (every service instantiation), not just when expired, and does not use `refreshOAuthTokens`, so it never goes through the sync endpoint. Further, the refreshed access token is saved but the Connection is built from the stale `credentialKey.access_token`. `response.statusText !== "OK"` is a fragile success check (HTTP/2 has empty statusText).

findings.title: Failure to parse refreshed tokens no longer logged/handled; parse now throws
findings.body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` throws on a parse failure, so the old zodError logging was removed and replaced by an exception. The following `tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data` check is now dead. In sync mode the minimal schema produces data without the `expires_in` transformation to an absolute timestamp, so the stored expiry is a relative offset.

findings.title: Webhook secret compared with non-constant-time `!==`; undefined header edge cases
findings.body: The secret is compared with `!==` (timing attack). If the header name env var is mis-set, or the secret is an empty string, the check is weak. Use `crypto.timingSafeEqual` and require method POST (no method check exists).

findings.title: Unhandled zod parse / decrypt / JSON.parse errors yield 500s; no method check
findings.body: `parse` throws on bad bodies and `symmetricDecrypt`/`JSON.parse` throw on bad payloads, all uncaught and returned as generic 500s instead of 400s. Use safeParse and try/catch. Also, the credential lookup uses `appId` only, so a user with several credentials for the same app gets an arbitrary one updated, and decrypted keys are not validated against any shape before being stored.

findings.title: APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is a string|undefined, not a boolean
findings.body: The constant evaluates to the key string (or undefined/""), not a boolean. This leaks the encryption key value into any module that might serialize/log the constant, and its type is misleading. Use `!!(...)`.

findings.title: Bigin passes credentialId as userId to refreshOAuthTokens
findings.body: `refreshAccessToken(credentialId, credentialKey)` passes `credentialId` as the `userId` argument. With sync enabled, the sync endpoint is asked about calcomUserId = credential id, fetching or syncing the wrong user's tokens. Pass `credential.userId`.

findings.title: Unrelated redirect URI change hardcodes slug
findings.body: The redirect URI was changed from `appConfig.slug` to a hardcoded "zoho-bigin" in add.ts only, while callback.ts still uses `appConfig.slug`. If they differ the OAuth redirect_uri will mismatch. This is unrelated to the PR.
